results.summary: This design is a standalone characterization platform for a single external resistive-switching device such as an RRAM, memristor, or phase-change cell. It drives an 8-bit DAC rail and reads back an 8-bit ADC rail, with four SPI-selectable modes: DC sweep with on-chip histogram and min/max tracking, pulse endurance with read-verify and fail-index latching, retention with periodic reads, and free-running mode. The design is implemented in mixed-signal style and is intended for silicon characterization of the external device. It requires an external resistive-switching device and an SPI host to control the modes and read results.

This design is a characterization platform for a single external memristor or RRAM device, providing DC sweep, pulse endurance, retention, and free-running modes. It uses an 8-bit DAC to drive the device and an 8-bit ADC to read back the response, with SPI control for mode selection and data readout. The design includes on-chip histogram and min/max tracking for DC sweeps, and read-verify with fail-index latching for endurance tests. It is implemented as a mixed-signal design and requires an external resistive-switching device and SPI host.

This design is a tensor processing unit inspired by Google's TPU that multiplies 8-bit floating-point matrices. It is implemented as a systolic array with a multiplier and accumulator, and is intended for machine learning inference. The design is written in Verilog and targets the Tiny Tapeout ASIC shuttle. It requires external control to load data and read results, likely via a microcontroller.

This design is a reimplementation of the Setun-1958 computer, a ternary-based machine, using Amaranth HDL. It reuses building blocks from the original implementation and is intended for educational or retro-computing purposes. The design requires a microcontroller to drive the pins and no other external hardware. It is written in Amaranth and targets the Tiny Tapeout ASIC shuttle.

This design is a game that outputs video via VGA, with graphics and display capabilities. It is written in Verilog and targets the Tiny Tapeout ASIC shuttle. The design requires a VGA monitor and possibly input devices such as buttons or a gamepad. It is notable for its retro-style graphics and gameplay.

This project is an RV32I RISC-V core implementation written in SystemVerilog, occupying a 4x4 tile area. No details about the microarchitecture, interfaces, or testing are provided, and no silicon results are reported. The design is intended for the Tiny Tapeout ASIC shuttle. It requires external control to load and run programs.

This design is a biomedical-oriented circuit that uses an SPI interface for communication. It includes a register file and scan-chain for testing, and is implemented in mixed-signal style. The design is intended for health monitoring applications and requires an external SPI host. No further details are provided.

This design is a neural network accelerator that performs inference using fixed-point arithmetic. It is implemented as a systolic array with a multiplier and accumulator, and is intended for machine learning applications. The design is written in Verilog and targets the Tiny Tapeout ASIC shuttle. It requires external control to load weights and input data.

This design is a finite state machine that implements a UART serial interface. It is written in Verilog and targets the Tiny Tapeout ASIC shuttle. The design requires an external UART host to communicate. It is notable for its simple and compact implementation.

This design is a characterization platform for memristor devices, using an SPI interface for control and data readout. It includes a DAC and ADC for analog signaling, and is implemented in mixed-signal style. The design is intended for testing resistive-switching devices and requires an external memristor and SPI host. It provides DC sweep and pulse endurance modes.
